body:
<!-- hive-mind-solve-repository-mode -->

## Objective

Address every open issue listed below in [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream) with a **single pull request**.

This issue was generated automatically by `/solve https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream` (repository mode). Native sub-issues and the complete closing-reference block below jointly define the required scope.

## Scope

- Open issues found in the repository: 7
- Issues requested in this single pull request: 7
- Issues selected for native sub-issue attachment: 7
- GitHub sub-issue limit per parent issue: 100

## Issues to address

- [ ] #226 Publish command-stream to crates.io through trusted publishing (remove CARGO_TOKEN) — opened 2026-10-13
- [ ] #227 $({ timeout }) is silently ignored: the command is never bounded (only signal works) — opened 2026-10-15
- [ ] #228 $ runs commands in a login shell (sh -l -c): profile reorders the caller's PATH (macOS path_helper) and prints into stdout — opened 2026-10-19
- [ ] #229 Rust: no way to remove a single inherited environment variable (`StreamingRunner`, `RunOptions`, `TerminalCaptureOptions`) — opened 2026-10-21
- [ ] #230 Rust: `StreamingRunner` / `OutputStream` has no live stdin pipe (argv + streaming + interactive input) — opened 2026-10-21
- [ ] #231 Terminal capture: no way to choose which artifacts are written (GIF always rendered in JS) — opened 2026-10-21
- [ ] #232 Fire-and-forget detached spawn (JS + Rust): start a command that outlives the caller and get its pid — opened 2026-10-21

## Requirements

1. Read every issue listed above (including its comments) and fully implement what it asks for.
2. Do all of the work in this single pull request. Do not defer any listed issue to a follow-up pull request.
3. The pull request description **must** close this issue and **every** issue listed above, so that merging the pull request closes all of them at once.
4. GitHub requires the full closing syntax for each issue: one keyword per issue. `Fixes #1, #2` only closes `#1`. Use the block below verbatim (plus `Fixes #<this issue>` for this issue).
5. If an issue turns out to be already resolved or not reproducible, say so explicitly in the pull request description — but still keep its closing reference so it is closed on merge.

## Required closing references in the pull request description

```
Fixes #226
Fixes #227
Fixes #228
Fixes #229
Fixes #230
Fixes #231
Fixes #232
```
title: Address all 7 open issues in link-foundation/command-stream
